name: drive-invoice-to-xero

trigger.authentication_note: Google Drive dennis@work.flowers. The SAME connection is needed twice: here on the trigger (which polls the folder) and as the `gdrive` alias in --connections, because the workflow code renames the file.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger (New File in Folder), one run per file added to the Invoices folder. No webhook_url — nothing external needs a catch URL, so there is no cutover step beyond turning the classic Zap off. Disabling the workflow moves the trigger to `released`; re-enabling reclaims it as `active` (verified 2026-07-28).

connectionless_apps.AICLIAPI: get_completion — authentication_id "0" (Included in Plan), no connection
connectionless_apps.ZapierTables: read via sdk.listTableRecords, not a TableCLIAPI action — no connection and no task cost

version_pinning_note: @zapier/zapier-durable 0.11.0 was npm-latest at build time but only ~20h old. The runtime installs with pnpm --config.minimumReleaseAge=1440, so a dependency younger than 24h fails at RUN time, not publish. Pinned to 0.10.1.

xero.organization_note: Used both as the `organization` input on Xero actions and as the `Xero-Tenant-Id` header on the raw request. _zap_raw_request has NO `organization` field in its schema (additionalProperties: false) and silently strips one — org-scoped calls fail with 'Please select an organization to perform this step on.' unless the header is set.
xero.bill_number_note: Zapier's new_bill `number` field maps to Xero's InvoiceNumber (not Reference) — verified against bills the classic Zap created.

bank_transactions.name: Xero Bank Transactions
bank_transactions.role: Read-only here. The match source for 'has this invoice already been paid?'. Chosen over a live Xero API query because Table reads cost no tasks.
bank_transactions.owned_by: the durable workflow `xero-bank-transactions-to-zapier-table` (019fa885-7d5e-73a8-b601-4ec31290bf4a), which replaced the classic Zap 'Process New Reconciled Transactions'
bank_transactions.coupling_warning: This workflow is only as correct as that one is current. The predecessor classic Zap's create step was paused on 2026-07-28, so the Table fell ~5 days behind: 7 of 43 live SPEND transactions in 2026-06-01..2026-07-28 were missing, all of them the newest. The visible symptom was NOT an error — it was duplicate draft bills in Xero, deleted by hand. That gap is NOT being backfilled, by design (a polling trigger primes its dedupe on first poll); see the feeder's known_gaps.
bank_transactions.table_stale_flag_note: `tableStale` measures the Table's OWN freshness as of 019fad1c: a `latest-bank-transaction` step reads the newest row (free — no filters, sort date desc, pageSize 1) and the flag trips when it is more than TABLE_STALE_AFTER_DAYS (14) behind the stepped `today`. An unreadable newest row also counts as stale, since an empty table, a renamed column and a failed read are indistinguishable from this side. The run output also carries `tableLagDays`, `tableLatestRowDate` and `windowRowsConsidered` so a run can be judged without re-querying.
bank_transactions.table_stale_flag_history: Before 019fad1c the flag was `windowRows === 0` — whether the invoice's own match window came back empty. That is a much weaker question: the window is [min(invoiceDate,dueDate)-7, max(invoiceDate,dueDate)+7], so for a freshly received unpaid invoice on 31-day terms it is [D-7, D+38] and ~39 of 46 days lie in the FUTURE where no transaction can exist. It therefore only inspected an ~8-day past slice, in which 'no payments recorded this week' is indistinguishable from 'feeder dead'. It misfired both ways in one day (2026-07-29): INV-26-0007 set tableStale true against a demonstrably healthy feeder (published 2026-07-28T11:39:22Z, trigger active, zero runs because no new Xero bank transaction had been CREATED since 2026-07-21), while INV-26-0006 read false only because one CPF row sat on its boundary date. The 14-day threshold sits deliberately above the largest legitimate quiet stretch observed, 8 days over 2026-07-21..2026-07-29.

vendor_payment_details.name: Vendor Payment Details
vendor_payment_details.role: WRITTEN here, one row per Xero contact, from the second AI call's payment-instruction fields. Read by the durable `xero-bill-approved-to-wise-transfer` to build a Wise recipient. Exists because Xero cannot hold a payment instruction: BankAccountDetails is a single free-text field, while Wise needs details.accountNumber and details.iban as different keys on different account types, and a sort code / ABA routing number / Singapore bank code all land in different places.
vendor_payment_details.owned_by: this workflow writes columns 1-21 and the provenance/flag columns; `xero-bill-approved-to-wise-transfer` is the SOLE writer of the five wise_recipient_* columns. Disjoint column sets, so no merge rule is needed between the two Zaps.

write_classes.money_identity: account_number, iban, swift_bic, bank_code, branch_code, paynow_identifier — filled when empty; a disagreement sets needs_review + conflict_note and changes NOTHING else, not even other empty fields.
write_classes.descriptive: account_holder_name, vendor_legal_type, account_type, account_currency, bank_country_code, paynow_identifier_type, bank_code_label — filled when empty, never overwritten; drift is reported in the run output but does NOT raise needs_review.
write_classes.correctable: xero_contact_name, bank_name, bank_address, payment_method, beneficiary_* — fill a gap or fix drift, never blank. None can redirect a payment.
write_classes.provenance: source_file_id, source_file_name, source_invoice_number, first_seen — written once.
write_classes.counters: last_seen and confirmations, always updated EXCEPT on a contradiction, which is not a corroboration.

vendor_payment_details.split_rationale: Freezing every field and alarming on any difference sounds safer and is worse: a vendor reformatting its own name would raise a fraud alert, and an alert that fires on formatting is an alert nobody reads. Nothing frozen is ever overwritten either way — what differs is what a disagreement MEANS.
vendor_payment_details.coupling_warning: This is the fraud boundary for anything that pays a vendor. A changed account number is NEVER applied: needs_review goes up and the account_number column keeps its stored value. When a wise_recipient_id is already cached the outcome escalates to conflict-blocked and the payment Zap refuses to prepare anything for that vendor until a human clears the flag. Clearing it means verifying out of band — phone the vendor on a number you already had, never one printed on the new invoice — then EITHER blanking the three flag columns (keep old details) OR blanking the frozen tuple AND all five wise_recipient_* columns AND the flags (accept the change). A half-cleared row reads as a never-seen vendor.
vendor_payment_details.normalisation_note: Comparison goes through normalizeAccountNumber. The live Wise recipient for Eugene Thuraisingam Asia LLC stores 0721445433 while their invoice prints 072-144543-3 — the same account. Without normalising, every Singapore vendor's second invoice would raise a false alarm.
vendor_payment_details.paynow_note: 9 of the 14 active recipients on the live Wise account are PayNow aliases rather than bank accounts, so for most vendors here PayNow is the only payable rail. Wise returns the alias HASHED (details.identifierAliasHash) and never in plaintext, which is why the payment Zap's cache binds on wise_recipient_alias_hash for that rail and on wise_recipient_account_number for bank rails.
vendor_payment_details.known_gap: No Xero contact id means no key, so no row: the ambiguous, deferred-to-new-bill and suppressed-* contact paths write nothing. Only deferred-to-new-bill loses anything real, and only for a brand-new vendor whose invoice prints a PayNow alias and nothing else at all — any bank account forces a contact create, which yields an id.
vendor_payment_details.failure_mode: A Table error is caught and reported as vendorPaymentRow.outcome 'error'; the bill is still raised. Bookkeeping must never cost a bill.

ai_model.calls_note: TWO AI steps, both standard/auto: `extract-invoice` (INVOICE_PROMPT, 21 output fields, the invoice header + line items) and `extract-payment-details` (PAYMENT_PROMPT, 16 output fields, how the vendor wants to be paid). Total AI cost is 2 tasks per invoice.
ai_model.why_two_calls: The payment fields were first folded into the single existing call, taking it from 21 output fields to 34, and that measurably broke the HEADER. A/B on 2026-07-02 Slack Technologies Limited, same tier and same PDF, six runs each: correct vendor name 6/6 at 21 fields versus 2/6 at 34. The four failures returned 'Company Flow Pte. Ltd.' — our own entity — as the vendor, with Vendor Country: Singapore to match; that invoice has a two-column header and under field pressure the model stopped resolving which column was which. Vendor Name binds the Xero contact AND the draft bill, so a header error raises a bill against the wrong party, whereas a missing bank detail merely stops a payment. INVOICE_PROMPT and OUTPUT_FIELDS are therefore left byte-for-byte as previously deployed and verified.
ai_model.tier_note: The header regression looks like a tier problem and is not one: the fix was splitting the call, not buying a better model. Standard at 21 fields scored 6/6. Upgrading to advanced/auto would have cost 3x per run and left the same design fault in place. Tier drives task cost: standard 1x, advanced 3x, premium 5x (plus the same multiplier per tool call; neither step makes any). Those three sentinels are the only valid values — anything else errors with 'Unknown tier sentinel'. Re-run the README's verified tables before changing tier.
ai_model.vendor_input_note: The payment call receives the vendor name resolved by the first call as its own `Vendor` input field, alongside the PDF. That is what makes a payment-only prompt safe: without it, a prompt that never reasons about the header cannot tell the vendor's remittance block from the recipient's own bank details, which most invoices also print. Passed as an input field rather than interpolated into the instructions so the prompt text stays static and scripts/check-prompts.mjs can verify it verbatim.
ai_model.required_fields_note: EVERY output field on BOTH calls is isRequired: true. AI by Zapier omits an isRequired:false output field from the structured response entirely — the model is never asked for it. Verified: an early run returned only the nine required fields from an invoice that plainly printed an address, phone, UEN and bank account. The prompts carry the counterweight, that an empty string is always acceptable and is the right answer when the invoice does not state the value.
ai_model.code_side_derivations: Two values are derived in code rather than by loosening the prompts, because both are exact: (1) bank_country_code from characters 5-6 of the SWIFT/BIC, which ARE the ISO-3166 country code by definition (CMFGUS33 -> US) — the prompt rightly forbids inferring a country from a currency or phone code, which otherwise left the US invoices with no corridor at all; (2) vendor_legal_type BUSINESS from a company suffix on the account holder name, which only ever upgrades Unknown and never contradicts a stated answer or guesses PRIVATE from a bare name.
ai_model.prompt_sync_note: scripts/check-prompts.mjs was extended to support more than one prompt per directory: a markdown file declares which literal it owns with an '<!-- embed: NAME_PROMPT -->' marker above its '## Prompt' heading. Previously the script matched only the FIRST *_PROMPT literal in a file, so two prompts in one Zap would each be compared against the same literal and --fix would overwrite it from every markdown in turn. Backwards compatible: a directory with a single prompt needs no marker, and the three Zaps that predate this are untouched.
ai_model.file_input_note: The PDF is passed to the model as a file input (inputFieldConfig_Invoice_isFileUrl), using the Drive trigger's `file` hydrate reference. Standard reads rendered PDFs directly, so no Files by Zapier text-extraction step is needed — which is what makes the line-item table legible.
ai_model.verified_note: Payment extraction validated on 9 real PDFs via the offline run-action harness, 2026-07-30 — see the README's 'Payment-instruction extraction' table. All 16 fields present in every response; all self-consistency checks passed. Two prompt bugs were caught and fixed there: an account number appearing in Vendor Bank Code labelled 'Ac No.', and a PayNow type of Unknown with a blank alias.

matching.rule: vendor (legal-suffix-normalised) AND exact total AND same currency AND SPEND, within +/-7 days of the invoice date or its due date
matching.note: Amount and currency are REQUIRED, not tiebreakers as the classic Zap's Agent had it. Anthropic had 3 transactions within 4 days of one invoice (104.58 / 133.58 / 99.00) — only the amount distinguishes the right one. SimplePay bills SGD 12 every month, so the date window is what stops a match against the wrong month. A split payment (Aspire FT 45.90 settled by 4.92 + 40.98) correctly fails to match rather than attaching to half of it.

description: Invoice PDF added to the Google Drive Invoices folder -> ONE AI by Zapier call extracts the header and the line items -> rename the file to '<invoice date> <vendor>' -> look for a matching SPEND bank transaction in the Xero Bank Transactions Zapier Table. Matched: attach the PDF to that transaction in Xero. Not matched: raise a DRAFT bill (guarded against duplicates by invoice number). Migration of the classic Zap 'Record New Bills in Xero'. Replaces its AI Agent step with deterministic code, requires an amount+currency match rather than treating amount as optional, merges its two AI calls into one, and reconciles extracted line items against the invoice total so a draft bill always adds up.
determinism_note: The workflow body runs in the durable runtime's GUARDED mode, where `Date` is replaced by a Proxy whose `construct` trap throws DeterminismViolation *before* it inspects its arguments — so a deterministic `new Date(Date.UTC(y, m, d))` is rejected just as hard as a clock read. Version 019fa878 had three such calls in the guarded body and failed on EVERY PDF invoice (`toIsoDate` threw on the first line after the AI step); the only path that worked was the non-PDF skip, which returns before reaching it, and that was the one end-to-end test run before publishing. Date handling is now integer arithmetic — `Date` is not referenced anywhere in the file, `Date.UTC` included, even though the Proxy's `get` trap leaves it unguarded — and the clock is read inside a `today` step. Verified against native `Date` across 47,847 days (1970..2100) in both directions before publishing.

version_history.note: Replace the tableStale tripwire. It now measures the Table's own freshness — a new free `latest-bank-transaction` step reads the newest row (sort date desc, pageSize 1) and the flag trips at more than TABLE_STALE_AFTER_DAYS (14) behind the stepped `today` — instead of asking whether the invoice's match window came back empty, which for a freshly received invoice is mostly a future-dated window and so misfired both ways on 2026-07-29. See tables.bank_transactions.table_stale_flag_history. The `today` step is now UNCONDITIONAL (it previously ran only when the model gave no usable invoice date) because the lag needs today on every run; it costs no task. Adds `tableLagDays`, `tableLatestRowDate` and `windowRowsConsidered` to the run output. No task-cost change: Table reads are free. Published from draft 019fad1b (base 019fab74) so trigger, connections, dependency pins and enabled state carried over from live. Validated before publish: tsc clean; no `Date` reference outside the stepped `today` clock read; the new logic lifted verbatim into a throwaway private durable and run against the real Table in the real 0.10.1 runtime — returned today 2026-07-29, latestRowDate 2026-07-21, tableLagDays 8, tableStale FALSE, i.e. the correct verdict under the exact conditions that made the old heuristic report true. Verified after publish: deployed source byte-matches workflow.ts, trigger status active on folder 14Rpcj…, enabled true, 0 open drafts. NOT yet exercised by a live PDF run.

Initial migration. Failed on every PDF invoice with DeterminismViolation — see determinism_note. Its one and only run (019fa97a, 2026-07-28T16:06:14Z) was Lantern Labs INV-26-0006, which therefore needed a manual replay on 019faae7.

Fix the guarded-mode `new Date()` calls: integer date arithmetic (`daysFromCivil`/`isoDateFromEpochMs`/`daysInMonth`), clock moved into a `today` step. `toIsoDate` now genuinely rejects an impossible date — the old NaN check never fired, because Date.UTC normalises overflow instead of failing, so a month like `2026-13-05` was handed straight to Xero as a bill date. Verified by replaying the failed Lantern Labs run: draft bill 99ea5905-aa60-4327-bcb7-984c1013e3e3.

Vendor-contact resolution on the create-bill branch. Before raising a bill the workflow lists Xero contacts (one GET /Contacts, 130 rows in a single page) and resolves the vendor with the same normalizeVendor/vendorMatches pair used for bank transactions: one match -> bind the bill to the contact's STORED name and fill only its EMPTY fields; several matches -> change nothing, log for a human merge; no match -> create the contact with the address, phone, tax number and bank details read off the invoice. `new_bill` has no contact-id input, so binding by the resolved name is the whole point — passing the invoice's spelling is what minted the four duplicate contact pairs. Bank details are write-once: a stored account is never overwritten, and a disagreement is reported as `contact.bankConflict` rather than applied, because an emailed invoice asking to be paid into a new account is what invoice-redirection fraud looks like. Contacts are written through _zap_raw_request (Zapier's `contact` action flattens to a single address). Also makes every vendor-detail output field isRequired: true — AI by Zapier drops an isRequired: false output field from the structured response entirely, which is why header.vendorEmail was always null in 019faae7. Published from a draft (019fab72) so the trigger, connections, dependency pins and enabled state were carried over from live rather than retyped. Validated before publish: tsc clean; 47 offline assertions against the real 130-contact ledger with the resolver transpiled out of workflow.ts; no `Date` reference outside the stepped `today` clock read; every sdk.* call inside a ctx.step. EXERCISED LIVE 2026-07-29 by run 019fac4a (Lantern Labs INV-26-0007, SGD 60.43) — 46s end to end, extraction 10/10 against the PDF, contact resolved via `exact` to the single existing record (no duplicate minted), enrichment `updated` filling tax number + address + phone, all three correct. Two controls closed by that run: (1) the bank-field control the README shipped as untested — INV-26-0007 offers ONLY a PayNow QR and a Wise link, and the model returned no bank account on a contact whose stored BankAccountDetails was empty, so a hallucinated account would have been written and reported; (2) toCurrencyCode normalising the model's raw `SGD$` (and `US$` on INV-26-0006) to an ISO code. Still unproven: header.vendorEmail — null on both live runs, correctly, because neither Lantern Labs invoice prints an email address.

Payment-instruction extraction as a SECOND AI step, feeding the new `Vendor Payment Details` Table (01KYR653H04DNMKKYAZ72534YG) that `xero-bill-approved-to-wise-transfer` reads to build a Wise recipient. Xero cannot hold the tuple — BankAccountDetails is one free-text field — so account number, IBAN, SWIFT, bank code + its printed label, branch code, account type, currency, bank address, account holder, legal type and the PayNow alias are stored per Xero contact instead. Written on BOTH finishing branches: the attach branch binds by the contact id already on the matched bank-transaction row (free), the bill branch by the resolved contact id. Bank details are write-once with the same discipline as the Xero field — a changed money-identity value sets needs_review and overwrites nothing, escalating to a hard stop the payment Zap obeys once a Wise recipient is cached. WHY A SECOND CALL: folding these fields into the existing extraction took it from 21 output fields to 34 and measurably broke the header — A/B on 2026-07-02 Slack Technologies Limited, same tier and PDF, correct vendor name 6/6 at 21 fields vs 2/6 at 34, the failures naming Company Flow Pte. Ltd. (our own entity) as the vendor. INVOICE_PROMPT and OUTPUT_FIELDS are therefore byte-identical to 019fad1c; this version is 745 pure insertions with zero deletions to the header path. Costs +1 task per invoice. Verified before publish: tsc clean; determinism grep clean (the only clock read remains inside ctx.step("today")); check-prompts in sync across 5 prompts; payment extraction scored on 9 real PDFs; 39 offline assertions on the upsert logic run against tsc's own emitted output. Published through a DRAFT (base 019fad1c), not publish-workflow-version, so the Drive trigger could not be silently unclaimed; verified after publish as triggers[0].status=active on folder 14Rpcj…, enabled=true, 0 open drafts, deployed source byte-identical to the repo. NOT YET EXERCISED BY A LIVE PDF — see live_runs.

draft-bill-created, invoice 99ea5905-aa60-4327-bcb7-984c1013e3e3. Manual replay of the failed run above with its original trigger payload. tableStale false (1 row: CPF 2026-07-21). No contact block — this version predates vendor-contact resolution. Extraction 10/10, including taking the invoice date 28/07/26 rather than the Billing Period start 03/07/26.

runs.invoice: Lantern Labs INV-26-0007, SGD 60.43, due 2026-08-29, FedEx pass-through
runs.outcome: draft-bill-created, invoice 1b61a648-859f-46e2-a430-fc5609d0f673. Email to bill 3m04s, fully hands-off. Extraction 10/10. Contact via `exact` -> 699fb6bb-960d-4a7f-ac43-3185e242890a, enrichment `updated`, filled [tax number, address, phone], no bankConflict. tableStale TRUE — a false positive against a healthy feeder; see tables.bank_transactions.table_stale_flag_note.

live_runs.known_gap_from_sequencing: INV-26-0006 is the invoice carrying Lantern Labs' remittance block (account 8311123520, SWIFT CMFGUS33, routing 026073008), and it ran on 019faae7, which had no contact logic. INV-26-0007 prints no bank details. So the Xero contact holds address, phone and UEN but NO bank account. Fill-empty-only means the next Lantern Labs invoice printing a remittance block will populate it.
live_runs.pending_verification: Version 019fb0f6 (payment-instruction extraction + Vendor Payment Details Table) has NOT yet been exercised by a live PDF, and neither had 019fad1c before it — this stacks an unproven version on an unproven one, on the Zap that writes to Xero. The next invoice into the Invoices folder is the real test. Watch for: two AI steps in the run (extract-invoice, extract-payment-details); a vendorPaymentRow block on the return object with outcome 'created'; and a matching row appearing in table 01KYR653H04DNMKKYAZ72534YG. A skip-path run proves nothing about any of it — that is exactly how the DeterminismViolation survived publishing in 019fa878.

replaces_classic_zap.title: Record New Bills in Xero
replaces_classic_zap.old_shape: Drive trigger -> PDFs-only filter -> AI invoice header -> rename -> AI Agent 'Xero Invoice Transaction Matcher' (run_behavior, App222036CLIAPI@3.1.0, agent d9d3381a-6aeb-4221-b5f4-3623f68ea7cc) -> Paths -> second AI call for line items -> Paths on tax -> two Create Bill branches / Upload Attachment
replaces_classic_zap.agent_note: The Agent searched this same Zapier Table as a knowledge source; it existed to do fuzzy vendor-name matching across legal suffixes. `normalizeVendor` does that in code for free. The Agent also missed matches that were present in the Table — SimplePay 1148057 SGD 12 had an exact same-day transaction and still got a duplicate bill.
